title: Preload the Material Symbols icon font so icons don't show loading artifacts on first load
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Start downloading the Material Symbols icon font while the page loads, instead of waiting until the first icon renders. Icons are part of the app's own UI and of many apps, so on a first (uncached) visit they often appear late, with visible loading artifacts until the font has downloaded.

### Why?

Material icons are now a common part of most apps:

- Streamlit's own UI uses them: the sidebar collapse and expand buttons, the main menu items, and the status widget.
- Many apps use them for page icons in `st.navigation` / `st.Page`, `icon=` on buttons, expanders, alerts and toasts, and `:material/...:` in Markdown.

The font is declared in `frontend/app/src/assets/css/fonts.css` with `font-display: block` and is about 375 KB. Browsers request an `@font-face` font only once text using it is laid out, so the download starts only after the JS bundle has run, the websocket has connected and the first icon has rendered. Until the font arrives, icons render as blank space. On slow connections, once the browser's block period (about 3 seconds) ends, the fallback font shows the icon's ligature name (for example `keyboard_double_arrow_left`) instead. Later visits hit the browser cache, so this mostly affects first loads, which is what new users see.

### How?

Start the download from the app's entry script with the CSS Font Loading API, instead of waiting for the first icon to render:

```ts
document.fonts.load('1em "Material Symbols Rounded"')
```

This needs no file name, so it can't go stale, and because it runs once the entry bundle has loaded, it doesn't compete with the JS the app needs for its first render.

Alternatives considered:

- **A `<link rel="preload">` in `index.html`**, as we do for Source Sans. That preload hard-codes the font's hashed file name, which works because Source Sans rarely changes. The `update-emojis-material-icons` workflow replaces the Material Symbols font every few weeks (28 times in 2026 so far), and each update changes its hash. Only the Vite build can compute that name, so a hard-coded preload would silently go stale. Keeping it current would need a build-time `index.html` transform or a frontend build inside the update script.
- **`fetchpriority="low"` on such a preload** would start the download even earlier, but it can't keep the font from competing with the JS. Over HTTP/1.1, the hint only delays when the request is sent, and the download then shares bandwidth.

The trade-off: every first visit downloads the font, even for apps that never show an icon.

title: Keep category colors stable across charts and badge columns when data is filtered
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Chart colors from `theme.chartCategoricalColors` are assigned by position, not by category. When a filter removes a category, the remaining ones can change color, so "Enterprise is indigo" holds on one rerun and not the next. Add a theme-aware way to pin a category to a palette slot, shared by charts and colored badge columns.

### Why?

Dashboards filter all the time, and readers learn colors as identities. Today the color a category gets depends on where it lands:

- **`st.echarts_chart`:** palette colors follow series order, and data order for pies and funnels. Removing the first series shifts every later series to a new color.
- **Built-in charts with `color=<column>`:** Vega-Lite picks colors from the values present in the data ("let Vega-Lite auto-assign colors" in `built_in_chart_utils.py`), so the mapping changes when a filter removes a value.
- **`MultiselectColumn(color="auto")`:** colors follow the position in `options`. That's stable only while every chart orders its categories the same way.

The only stable alternative is explicit hex colors, which ignore the light/dark theme palettes. Built-in charts and badge columns accept theme color names (`"red"`, `"blue"`, …), but not slots of `chartCategoricalColors`. ECharts specs accept neither.

In a BI demo ([feature-demos/bi-dashboard](https://github.com/streamlit/feature-demos/tree/main/bi-dashboard)), keeping plan colors stable under a plan filter meant keeping every plan's series in every chart, with null data when filtered out:

```python
series = [
    {
        "name": plan,
        "type": "line",
        "stack": "mrr",
        # A filtered-out plan keeps its series (and color slot) but draws nothing.
        "data": values[plan].tolist() if plan in active_plans else [None] * len(months),
    }
    for plan in PLANS  # Fixed order = fixed colors.
]
```

### How?

Some options, from smallest to largest:

1. **Palette slot references** wherever Streamlit resolves colors: built-in chart `color` lists, `MultiselectColumn(color=[...])`, `ProgressColumn` and the chart columns, and `st.echarts_chart` specs. For example, `"chart:1"` (exact syntax open) would resolve on the frontend to the active theme's first categorical color, so it's correct in light and dark mode.
2. **A value-to-color mapping** for built-in charts and `MultiselectColumn`, for example `color={"Enterprise": "chart:1", "Pro": "chart:2", "Starter": "chart:3"}`, accepting slots, theme color names, or CSS colors.
3. **An app-wide category map**, set once (in config or a command) and applied to every chart and badge that colors by category.

Option 1 alone would fix ECharts specs and keep everything theme-aware. Option 2 would make the built-in charts stable without reshaping data.

### Additional Context

- Related: #12805 (theme colors in `st.map` and `st.pydeck_chart`), #11974 (`chartCategoricalColors` needs a reload for Plotly).
- Found while building [feature-demos/bi-dashboard](https://github.com/streamlit/feature-demos/tree/main/bi-dashboard) against `develop`.

title: Return item names in st.echarts_chart selections and index labels in ButtonColumn clicks
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

`st.echarts_chart` selections and `st.column_config.ButtonColumn` clicks report only positions (`data_indices` and `click.row`). To act on them, an app has to rebuild the exact order Streamlit received and map each position back to an entity. Include the selected item's name (and `id` when set) in ECharts selections, and the row's index label in `ButtonColumn` clicks.

### Why?

In a BI demo ([feature-demos/bi-dashboard](https://github.com/streamlit/feature-demos/tree/main/bi-dashboard)), every interactive element maps positions back to entities by hand:

- **Donut of revenue by industry** (click a slice to filter a table): `INDUSTRIES[i]` only works because the spec's `data` list was built in exactly that order.
- **Scatter with one series per plan** (brush to filter): indices are series-local, so the page rebuilds each plan's subset in the same row order as the spec.
- **Bars sorted by value** (click to filter): `totals.index[i]` from the same sorted Series that built the spec.
- **ButtonColumn row actions**: `table.index[click.row]`. In an `on_click` callback, the whole table has to go through `args=` so the callback can resolve the row.

```python
event = st.echarts_chart(spec, on_select="rerun")
selected = [
    INDUSTRIES[i]  # Must match the order used to build spec["series"][0]["data"].
    for group in event.selection.selected
    for i in group["data_indices"]
]
```

This mapping is easy to get subtly wrong, and the docstring warns that indices "are not revalidated against the new data" when `key` keeps a selection across spec changes. The other chart commands already return values: `st.plotly_chart` points include `x`, `y`, and `customdata`, and Vega-Lite selections report field values.

### How?

**ECharts:** Add `names` (and `ids` when data items set `id`) to each entry in `selection.selected`, aligned with `data_indices`:

```python
{
    "series_index": 0,
    "series_name": "Industry",
    "data_type": "main",
    "data_indices": [2],
    "names": ["Retail"],
}
```

ECharts already resolves this name: it's the `{b}` value in templates and `params.name` in events (the data item's `name`, or the category for category-axis series). The frontend could read it with `seriesData.getName(dataIndex)` when it builds the payload. For graph `edge` entries, the link's `source`/`target` might be more useful than a name.

**ButtonColumn:** Add `index` to `ButtonColumnClickState`, holding the clicked row's index label (a tuple for a `MultiIndex`, if serializable):

```python
click = st.session_state.deal_click
deal_id = click.index  # Instead of table.index[click.row].
```

The same idea could apply to `st.dataframe` row selections (`event.selection.rows` is positional too), but that can be a follow-up.

### Additional Context

- Related: #12395 (easier cross-filtering between charts and dataframes), #8914 (confusion over Plotly selection indices), #17627 (setting chart selections programmatically).
- Found while building [feature-demos/bi-dashboard](https://github.com/streamlit/feature-demos/tree/main/bi-dashboard) against `develop`.

- **Donut of revenue by industry** (click a slice to filter a table): `INDUSTRIES[i]` only works because the spec's `data` list was built in exactly that order.
- **Scatter with one series per plan** (brush to filter): indices are series-local, so the page rebuilds each plan's subset in the same row order as the spec.
- **Bars sorted by value** (click to filter): `totals.index[i]` from the same sorted Series that built the spec.
- **ButtonColumn row actions**: `table.index[click.row]`. In an `on_click` callback, the whole table has to go through `args=` so the callback can resolve the row.

```python
event = st.echarts_chart(spec, on_select="rerun")
selected = [
    INDUSTRIES[i]  # Must match the order used to build spec["series"][0]["data"].
    for group in event.selection.selected
    for i in group["data_indices"]
]
```

This mapping is easy to get subtly wrong, and the docstring warns that indices "are not revalidated against the new data" when `key` keeps a selection across spec changes. The other chart commands already return values: `st.plotly_chart` points include `x`, `y`, and `customdata`, and Vega-Lite selections report field values.

### How?

**ECharts:** Add `names` (and `ids` when data items set `id`) to each entry in `selection.selected`, aligned with `data_indices`:

```python
{
    "series_index": 0,
    "series_name": "Industry",
    "data_type": "main",
    "data_indices": [2],
    "names": ["Retail"],
}
```

ECharts already resolves this name: it's the `{b}` value in templates and `params.name` in events (the data item's `name`, or the category for category-axis series). The frontend could read it with `seriesData.getName(dataIndex)` when it builds the payload. For graph `edge` entries, the link's `source`/`target` might be more useful than a name.

**ButtonColumn:** Add `index` to `ButtonColumnClickState`, holding the clicked row's index label (a tuple for a `MultiIndex`, if serializable):

```python
click = st.session_state.deal_click
deal_id = click.index  # Instead of table.index[click.row].
```

The same idea could apply to `st.dataframe` row selections (`event.selection.rows` is positional too), but that can be a follow-up.

- Related: #12395 (easier cross-filtering between charts and dataframes), #8914 (confusion over Plotly selection indices), #17627 (setting chart selections programmatically).

title: Treat zero-valued string deltas like "+0.0 pts" as zero in st.metric
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

`st.metric` treats only the number `0` and the string `"0"` as a zero delta. A formatted string that is numerically zero, such as `"+0.0 pts"` or `"0.0%"`, gets a colored arrow. Treat a string delta as zero when its leading number is zero.

### Why?

The current rule is intentional (#15790 kept zero-looking strings positive, and #17029 documented it). It's still easy to hit in real dashboards:

- Formatted strings are the only way to show units on a delta today, because `format` is shared with `value` (see #17834). So most KPI cards pass strings.
- Rounding produces zero strings all the time. In a BI demo, the gross churn card showed a red up arrow (with `delta_color="inverse"`) for a change of about `+0.04` points, formatted as `"+0.0 pts"`.
- The documented workaround (pass the number `0`) requires a helper next to every formatting call, and the formatting code usually sits far from the `st.metric` call.

```python
import streamlit as st

st.metric("Monthly gross churn", "1.2%", f"{0.04:+.1f} pts", delta_color="inverse")
# Shows "+0.0 pts" with a red up arrow instead of a gray, arrow-less delta.
```

### How?

When `delta` is a string, read its leading signed number (after optional currency symbols and whitespace, for example `"+0.0 pts"`, `"0%"`, `"-0.00"`, `"$0"`). If that number equals zero, use the existing zero treatment: gray, no arrow. Other strings keep today's rules (a leading minus is negative, otherwise positive).

This changes behavior for zero-valued strings such as `"0%"`, which are green today. It updates `test_zero_like_strings_keep_positive_direction` and `test_negative_zero_string_is_negative`. A gray zero seems to be what authors expect, but if the change is too risky, #17834 (`delta_format`) would let apps pass numeric deltas with units, which avoids most of these strings.

### Additional Context

- Related: #15005 and #15790 (neutral zero delta), #17029 (documentation of the string rule), #17834 (`delta_format`).
- Found while building [feature-demos/bi-dashboard](https://github.com/streamlit/feature-demos/tree/main/bi-dashboard) against `develop`.

title: Add a separate delta_format to st.metric
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

`st.metric(format=...)` applies one format to both `value` and `delta`. A metric whose value and delta have different units, such as a dollar amount with a percent change, therefore can't use numeric inputs. Add a `delta_format` parameter so the delta can have its own format.

### Why?

KPI cards usually mix units: revenue with a percent change, a rate with a change in percentage points, a count with a "vs. last period" percent. While building a BI demo ([feature-demos/bi-dashboard](https://github.com/streamlit/feature-demos/tree/main/bi-dashboard)), none of the four KPI cards could use `format`. Each one formats both strings by hand:

```python
st.metric(
    "Annual recurring revenue",
    money(arr),  # "$21.44M"
    f"{arr_change:+.1%}",  # "+40.6%"
    delta_description="vs. 12 months ago",
)
st.metric(
    "Net revenue retention",
    f"{nrr:.1f}%",  # "125.5%"
    f"{nrr_change:+.1f} pts",  # "+13.0 pts"
)
```

Passing pre-formatted strings gives up the numeric handling of `delta`. Only the number `0` and the string `"0"` count as zero, so a change that rounds to zero still gets a colored arrow. The app needs a helper to turn those strings back into `0`; see #17835.

### How?

Add a keyword-only `delta_format` parameter that accepts the same values as `format` (`"percent"`, `"dollar"`, `"compact"`, printf-style strings, and the others). When it's `None` (default), the delta keeps using `format`, so existing apps don't change.

```python
st.metric("Revenue", 1_240_000, 0.084, format="dollar", delta_format="percent")
st.metric("Net revenue retention", 125.5, 13.0, format="%.1f%%", delta_format="%+.1f pts")
```

With numeric deltas, the existing zero, sign, and color rules keep working while the text shows the right unit.

### Additional Context

- Related: #12284 (precision for `"compact"` formatting), #17835 (zero-valued string deltas).
- Found while building [feature-demos/bi-dashboard](https://github.com/streamlit/feature-demos/tree/main/bi-dashboard) against `develop`.

title: st.cache_data(persist="disk") fails on every call after a cache file is left empty, since writes aren't atomic
description:
_Filed by Claude Code (an AI coding agent) on behalf of Aidan Feldman._

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`LocalDiskCacheStorage.set()` writes cache files in place, so a `.memo` file is empty while it's being written, and stays empty if the write doesn't finish. `get()` treats an empty (or otherwise unreadable) file as a `CacheStorageError` rather than a miss, so the cached function raises `CacheError: Unable to read from cache` on every call until the file is deleted by hand.

We hit this on a deployed app (Fly.io, one machine with a volume for the cache), where two entries of an async `st.cache_data(persist="disk")` function were left empty while it was being used for the first time. Every page that needed those entries failed until we deleted the files. We couldn't find why those writes didn't finish: there was no crash, OOM kill, or restart around them, and the disk wasn't full. A concurrent read during a write fails the same way (the logs showed that too).

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st


@st.cache_data(persist="disk")
def compute():
    return "value"


st.write(compute())
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `streamlit run app.py` and load the page, so the value is written to `~/.streamlit/cache`.
1. Stop the app, and empty the cache file, as an unfinished write leaves it: `for f in ~/.streamlit/cache/*.memo; do : > "$f"; done`
1. Start the app again and load the page.

### Expected Behavior

The unreadable entry is treated as a miss: `compute()` runs again and its result is stored.

### Current Behavior

The page fails, and keeps failing on every reload:

```
streamlit.errors.Error: Read zero byte file: ".../.streamlit/cache/807cfa4a7f24187109444108aac9df84-cae66941d9efbd404e4d88758ea67670.memo"
The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:
streamlit.runtime.caching.storage.cache_storage_protocol.CacheStorageError: Unable to read from cache
The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:
streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_errors.CacheError: Unable to read from cache
```

The same happens with async cached functions.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.66.1
- Python version: 3.14.6
- Operating System: macOS 27.2 (repro above) and Linux (Debian trixie, on Fly.io, where we hit it)
- Browser: n/a

### Additional Information

A possible fix, in `lib/streamlit/runtime/caching/storage/local_disk_cache_storage.py`:

1. In `set()`, write to a temporary file in the same folder and `os.replace()` it into place, so readers only ever see a complete file, and an interrupted write leaves the old entry (or none) rather than an empty one. On Windows, `os.replace()` can fail while another thread has the file open, which could be treated like the existing write failures (skip caching).
1. In `get()`, treat an empty file as a miss (`CacheStorageKeyNotFoundError`) and delete it, so it's recomputed. Truncated pickles failing in `cache_data_api.read_result()` could arguably be handled the same way.

As a workaround, we catch `CacheError`, call the function's `.clear()` with the same arguments, and call it again.

Possibly related: #16907, which proposes replacing `persist="disk"` with configurable storage.

title: Required widgets lose blocked empty UI state across remount (beyond text_area)
description:
## Summary

`st.text_area(required=True)` now persists a blocked empty edit across remounts via `WidgetStateManager` element state (#17737). Other required widgets still keep `dirty` / `hasRequiredError` (or equivalent) only in React `useState`, so the same sibling-rerun remount can snap a blocked empty field back to the last accepted value and drop the required error.

`specs/2026-08-18-required-widgets/product-spec.md` requires that a rerun from another widget must **not** snap a blocked empty field back (keep `dirty`).

## Widgets likely affected

- `st.text_input`
- `st.number_input`
- date / time / datetime inputs
- select widgets with required empty state

## Suggested fix

Reuse the TextArea pattern: persist the blocked UI value in element state while the required error shows, restore on mount, clear when leaving that state. Cover with remount unit tests.

## Related

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17737
- `specs/2026-08-18-required-widgets/product-spec.md`

title: Free-threaded Python: DeltaGenerator.__init__ rewrites mixin __module__ on every instance, serializing script threads
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

On free-threaded CPython 3.14 (GIL disabled), creating `DeltaGenerator` objects from more than one thread at a time is about 100–300× slower than from a single thread. `DeltaGenerator.__init__` reassigns `__module__` on every callable of every mixin each time an instance is created (`lib/streamlit/delta_generator.py`, lines 350–355 on `develop`), so concurrent script threads keep writing the same shared function objects. In a multi-session app this serializes all sessions, so a free-threaded server is currently slower than one with the GIL enabled.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import sys
import threading
import time

from streamlit.delta_generator import DeltaGenerator


def bench(n_threads: int, per_thread: int = 300) -> float:
    def work() -> None:
        for _ in range(per_thread):
            DeltaGenerator()

    threads = [threading.Thread(target=work) for _ in range(n_threads)]
    start = time.perf_counter()
    for t in threads:
        t.start()
    for t in threads:
        t.join()
    return n_threads * per_thread / (time.perf_counter() - start)


DeltaGenerator()  # warm up
print(f"GIL enabled: {sys._is_gil_enabled()}")
for n in (1, 2, 4, 8):
    print(f"{n} thread(s): {bench(n):>9,.0f} DeltaGenerator() per second")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install the free-threaded interpreter and Streamlit, e.g. `uv python install 3.14t`, then `pip install streamlit==1.66.1` in a 3.14t environment.
2. Run the script above with the GIL disabled: `PYTHON_GIL=0 python repro.py`.
3. For comparison, run it with the GIL enabled: `PYTHON_GIL=1 python repro.py`.

### Expected Behavior

With the GIL disabled, throughput should grow with the number of threads, or at least not collapse. Applying the one-line change under "Additional Information" gives exactly that (bottom row of the table).

### Current Behavior

Same script, same 16-core Linux node:

| | 1 thread | 2 threads | 4 threads | 8 threads |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `PYTHON_GIL=0`, Streamlit 1.66.1 | 12,043/s | **126/s** | **42/s** | **60/s** |
| `PYTHON_GIL=1`, Streamlit 1.66.1 | 11,796/s | 12,282/s | 14,513/s | 9,270/s |
| `PYTHON_GIL=0`, with the change below | 12,992/s | 18,854/s | 33,815/s | **60,967/s** |

The effect carries over to a real app. In a multi-session app whose pages auto-rerun a fragment every 2 s, with 50 simulated concurrent sessions over the WebSocket protocol for 300 s, we currently have to run the server with `-X gil=1`. In that mode only 1.4% of the fragment reruns completed before the next one was due. With the GIL disabled and this change applied, all of them completed (median 38 ms), with server CPU peaking at about 6 cores.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.66.1 (the loop is unchanged on `develop` as of 2026-10-31)
- Python version: CPython 3.14.8, free-threading build
- Operating System: Linux (RHEL 8, kernel 4.18), 16 cores
- Browser: not relevant

### Additional Information

Proposed fix: skip the assignment when the value is already correct. Behavior is unchanged, because after the first instance every mixin function already has `__module__ == "streamlit.delta_generator"`, and the line still runs whenever the value differs.

```diff
         for mixin in self.__class__.__bases__:
             for func in mixin.__dict__.values():
-                if callable(func):
+                if callable(func) and func.__module__ != self.__module__:
                     func.__module__ = self.__module__
```

I found no other per-element function-attribute writes in `lib/streamlit`. Related: #13064 (general free-threading support).

title: st.dataframe with a fixed pixel height does not show all rows in fullscreen mode
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When `st.dataframe` gets a fixed pixel height (e.g. `height=458` to show 12 rows), opening it in fullscreen mode keeps that height. Only the first rows are visible, the rest of the screen stays empty and the table has to be scrolled inside the fullscreen view. Expected: in fullscreen the table uses the available height (up to all rows), as it does with the default height.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": range(40), "b": range(40)})
st.dataframe(df, height=(12 + 1) * 35 + 3)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the script.
2. Click the fullscreen button in the table's toolbar.

### Expected Behavior

The table fills the fullscreen height and shows as many rows as fit (here all 40).

### Current Behavior

The table keeps its 458 px height in fullscreen: 12 rows visible, the rest of the screen empty, a vertical scrollbar inside the table.

From reading the bundled frontend (`DataFrame.*.js`, the table sizer hook): on expand, the height is set to the full content height, but the layout effect that depends on the measured container height runs again when the element's size changes on entering fullscreen and resets the height to the fixed pixel value. (Our reading of the minified code, not verified in a debugger.)

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.66.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Linux (server), viewed on Windows 10
- Browser: Chrome

title: Add `required` parameter to `st.radio`
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add `required: bool = False` to `st.radio`, so a form with a radio that starts empty (`index=None`) can't be submitted until the user picks an option. This is a follow-up from the [required-widgets spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/specs/2026-08-18-required-widgets/product-spec.md) (#16555), which shipped `required` on the text, number, date/time, and selectbox widgets (#7165).

### Why?

Radio groups without a preselected option are common in forms (survey questions, "Choose a plan"), because a preselected answer biases the result. Today `st.radio(..., index=None)` lets the form submit `None`, and the app has to reject it after the rerun.

### How?

Proposed behavior, from the spec:

- **Empty** means `None` (`index=None`). `required=True` doesn't change the default: a radio still starts on the first option unless you pass `index=None`.
- **Form submit:** blocked while nothing is selected (no rerun, no `clear_on_submit`). The radio group shows `This field is required.` with the same error chrome as the other required widgets (error icon with tooltip and a red outline; exact placement on the group to be settled in design), a visually hidden `role="alert"` linked by `aria-describedby`, and `aria-invalid` on the `radiogroup`. The submit button is not disabled.
- **Outside a form:** users can't deselect a radio, so `required` adds the muted `(required)` label marker and `aria-required="true"` on the `radiogroup`.
- **Same as the shipped widgets:** the return type stays `V | None`, `required` is part of the widget ID only when there is no `key`, it works with `on_change="ignore"`, and the check runs in the browser only.

```python
with st.form("survey"):
    plan = st.radio("Plan", ["Free", "Pro", "Team"], index=None, required=True)
    if st.form_submit_button("Continue"):
        st.write(f"Selected {plan}")
```

### Additional Context

- Spec: [required-widgets product spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/specs/2026-08-18-required-widgets/product-spec.md), sections "Enforcement styles" (selection widgets), "Design", and "Accessibility".
- Umbrella request: #7165.

title: Add `required` parameter to `st.multiselect`
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add `required: bool = False` to `st.multiselect`, meaning at least one option must be selected. This is a follow-up from the [required-widgets spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/specs/2026-08-18-required-widgets/product-spec.md) (#16555), which shipped `required` on the text, number, date/time, and selectbox widgets (#7165).

### Why?

Many forms need "pick at least one" (tags, regions, recipients). Today an empty multiselect submits the form, and outside a form, removing the last option reruns the app with `[]`.

### How?

Proposed behavior, from the spec:

- **Empty** means `[]`. `required=True` doesn't change the default.
- **Form submit:** blocked while nothing is selected (no rerun, no `clear_on_submit`). The widget shows `This field is required.` with the same error chrome as the other required widgets: red outline, error icon with tooltip, and a visually hidden `role="alert"` linked by `aria-describedby`. The submit button is not disabled.
- **Can't return to empty:** once at least one option is selected, the last one can't be removed. The remove button on the last chip and the clear-all button are hidden, and Backspace doesn't remove it either. Users can add another option first and then remove the old one.
- **`max_selections=1` with `required=True`:** the last-option lock plus the existing "Remove an option first" limit means the user can't swap the only selection. The spec keeps the same lock here (no swap shortcut and no error); call it out in the changelog. `st.selectbox(..., required=True)` is the alternative for a single required choice.
- **Label and accessibility:** a muted `(required)` marker when the label is visible, and `aria-required="true"`.
- **Same as the shipped widgets:** the return type stays `list[V]` (no non-empty guarantee, since the widget returns its default until the user picks), `required` is part of the widget ID only when there is no `key`, it works with `on_change="ignore"`, and the check runs in the browser only.

```python
with st.form("share"):
    recipients = st.multiselect("Recipients", team, required=True)
    if st.form_submit_button("Share"):
        share(recipients)
```

### Additional Context

- Spec: [required-widgets product spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/specs/2026-08-18-required-widgets/product-spec.md), sections "Enforcement styles" (selection widgets) and "Edge cases".
- `min_selections` (#9977) stays separate. `required=True` is the `min_selections=1` case.
- Umbrella request: #7165.

This is a follow-up from the [required-widgets spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/specs/2026-08-18-required-widgets/product-spec.md) (#16555), which shipped `required` on the text, number, date/time, and selectbox widgets (#7165).

### Why?

Many forms need "pick at least one" (tags, regions, recipients). Today an empty multiselect submits the form, and outside a form, removing the last option reruns the app with `[]`.

### How?

Proposed behavior, from the spec:

- **Empty** means `[]`. `required=True` doesn't change the default.
- **Form submit:** blocked while nothing is selected (no rerun, no `clear_on_submit`). The widget shows `This field is required.` with the same error chrome as the other required widgets: red outline, error icon with tooltip, and a visually hidden `role="alert"` linked by `aria-describedby`. The submit button is not disabled.
- **Can't return to empty:** once at least one option is selected, the last one can't be removed. The remove button on the last chip and the clear-all button are hidden, and Backspace doesn't remove it either. Users can add another option first and then remove the old one.
- **`max_selections=1` with `required=True`:** the last-option lock plus the existing "Remove an option first" limit means the user can't swap the only selection. The spec keeps the same lock here (no swap shortcut and no error); call it out in the changelog. `st.selectbox(..., required=True)` is the alternative for a single required choice.
- **Label and accessibility:** a muted `(required)` marker when the label is visible, and `aria-required="true"`.
- **Same as the shipped widgets:** the return type stays `list[V]` (no non-empty guarantee, since the widget returns its default until the user picks), `required` is part of the widget ID only when there is no `key`, it works with `on_change="ignore"`, and the check runs in the browser only.

```python
with st.form("share"):
    recipients = st.multiselect("Recipients", team, required=True)
    if st.form_submit_button("Share"):
        share(recipients)
```

- `min_selections` (#9977) stays separate. `required=True` is the `min_selections=1` case.
- Umbrella request: #7165.

title: Align `required` on `st.pills` and `st.segmented_control` with other input widgets
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

`st.pills` and `st.segmented_control` have had `required` since 1.56 (#14414), but it only stops the user from deselecting a single-select option. Align it with the `required` parameter the other input widgets now have from the [required-widgets spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/specs/2026-08-18-required-widgets/product-spec.md) (#16555): a `(required)` label marker, form-submit gating, and multi-select support.

### Why?

`required` should mean the same thing on every widget. Today a required pills or segmented control that starts empty (no `default`) still lets a form submit with `None`, shows no `(required)` marker, and `required=True` with `selection_mode="multi"` raises an error (#14900).

### How?

From the spec's "Pills and segmented_control" section:

| Today | Proposed |
| --- | --- |
| Can't deselect once a value is selected | Unchanged |
| May start empty when `default` is unset | Unchanged; don't auto-select the first option |
| No `(required)` label | Add the marker when the label is visible; keep `aria-required` |
| An empty required widget can still submit a form | Block the submit and show `This field is required.` with the shared error chrome (red outline, error icon with tooltip, visually hidden `role="alert"`) |
| `required=True` with `selection_mode="multi"` raises | Allow it: at least one selection, and the last selected option can't be deselected |

Also:

- **Widget identity:** `required` is not part of the widget ID today. Match the other required widgets: include it only when there is no `key`.
- **Typing:** keep the existing overloads that narrow the return type when `required=True` and `default` is set. Multi-select with `required` still returns `list[V]`.
- **Behavior change:** an empty required pills or segmented control inside a form will start blocking the submit. Call this out in the changelog.

### Additional Context

- Spec: [required-widgets product spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/specs/2026-08-18-required-widgets/product-spec.md), section "Pills and segmented_control (existing `required`)".
- This includes #14900 (`required` for multi-select pills).
- #9870: the original single-select request, shipped in 1.56.
- Umbrella request: #7165.

title: Add `required` parameter to `st.file_uploader`, `st.camera_input`, and `st.audio_input`
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add `required: bool = False` to `st.file_uploader`, `st.camera_input`, and `st.audio_input`, so a form can't be submitted until a file or recording is provided. This is a follow-up from the [required-widgets spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/specs/2026-08-18-required-widgets/product-spec.md) (#16555), which shipped `required` on the text, number, date/time, and selectbox widgets (#7165).

### Why?

Upload forms usually can't continue without a file ("upload a CSV, then ingest it"). Today an empty uploader submits the form. Checking for `None` afterwards in Python costs a rerun, and with `clear_on_submit=True` the other fields are already wiped by the time the app rejects the submit. These widgets also commit empty today: deleting the last file or clearing a recording reruns the app with `None`.

### How?

Proposed behavior, from the spec's "File-like widgets" section:

- **Empty** means `None`, or `[]` with `accept_multiple_files`. An upload still in flight is not empty.
- **Form submit:** blocked while the widget is empty (no rerun, no `clear_on_submit`). The widget shows `This field is required.` with the same error chrome as the other required widgets: red outline, error icon with tooltip, and a visually hidden `role="alert"` linked by `aria-describedby`. The submit button is not disabled.
- **`st.file_uploader`:** deleting the last remaining file is locked, so the widget can't go back to empty. Dropping a new file still replaces it.
- **`st.camera_input` / `st.audio_input`:** keep the Clear button, because it is how the user recaptures, but Clear no longer commits `None`. The next capture commits.
- **Label and accessibility:** a muted `(required)` marker when the label is visible. The dropzone, camera, and audio roots don't honor `aria-required`, so `(required)` also goes into the accessible name (`aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).
- **Same as the shipped widgets:** the return type does not narrow, `required` is part of the widget ID only when there is no `key`, and the check runs in the browser only.

```python
with st.form("upload"):
    f = st.file_uploader("CSV", type="csv", required=True)
    if st.form_submit_button("Ingest"):
        ingest(f)
```

### Additional Context

- Spec: [required-widgets product spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/specs/2026-08-18-required-widgets/product-spec.md), sections "Enforcement styles" (file-like widgets) and "Accessibility".
- Umbrella request: #7165.
- The existing behavior that disables the form submit button while an upload is in flight stays as it is.

title: Proposal: a source-linked claim review component
description:
### Summary

I would like to build a Streamlit component for reviewing individual claims against source passages. A reviewer would select a claim, see the exact referenced span, and return an accept/reject/edit decision to Python.

### Proposed first version

I would start with a plain-text document with stable span coordinates and ten claims. The component would preserve claim IDs, support keyboard navigation, and return structured edits and review statuses. I would treat source support as a human decision and avoid presenting the component as an automatic truth checker.

Would this be a useful ecosystem component, and is there an existing gallery project covering the same interaction? I can develop a small package and example app if the scope fills a gap.

### Background

I have experience taking a new upstream direction from [maintainer agreement](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/11704) to reviewed implementation, including Qwen Code's merged [Android connection profiles](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/12121).

title: Minimal toolbar with running man animation
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

if I set toolbarmode to minimal to remove the distracting 3 dots menu, I also loose the running man animation. This animation is quite useful as a feedback that the system is 'running' and the user needs to wait for the streamlit page reload to complete. 

### Why?

This becomes particularly acute for heavy apps / time taking interactions, where running man animation gives psychological reaffirmation for the user to patiently wait. 3 dots menu (in its current non customisable shape) is mostly not useful in prod environment and hence the need to set toolbar mode to minimal. But that causes a side effect where I loose the running man animation

### How?

few ideas in mind - 
 - Config.toml - toolbar mode supports "no_menu" mode so that it only disables the 3dot menu w/o disabling the loader.
 - Config.toml has a distinct key for toggling on/off loader visibility - this would work nicely with the existing "minimal" mode of toolbar mode. so if loader is disabled while toolbar is minimal, toolbar completely disappears, otherwise if loader is enabled on minimal toolbar, then we only see the loader in toolbar not the 3 dot menu.
 - set page config also can potentially support enabling/disabling loader - but I wouldnt prefer this since it will force us to enable/disable this per page instead of on the entire app

### Additional Context

### Summary

BUG Report.The bug starts when you want to replace the previous toast with a new one, following the Streamlit documentation:

import time
import streamlit as st

def cook_breakfast():
    msg = st.toast("Gathering ingredients...")
    time.sleep(1)
    msg.toast("Cooking...")
    time.sleep(1)
    msg.toast("Ready!", icon="🥞")

title: Lazy-load unevaluated data objects in `st.dataframe` instead of cutting them off
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

`st.dataframe` still truncates most unevaluated inputs to 10,000 rows and shows a "showing only …" warning. Polars `LazyFrame` already loads on demand; the other types we treat as unevaluated should do the same out of the box, with no cutoff and no manual `to_pandas()` / `collect()` / `compute()`.

### Why?

These objects are used because the data lives on the backend (Snowflake, Spark, DuckDB, …) and is too large to materialize. The cutoff forces a full collect or hand-rolled pagination, which defeats passing a Snowpark table or similar straight into `st.dataframe`.

### How?

Reuse the existing lazy path: above the current 10k cutoff, fetch rows from the backend as the user scrolls. `lazy=False` keeps today's preview.

```python
orders = session.table("orders")  # Snowpark Table
st.dataframe(orders)
```

Still cut off today (`is_unevaluated_data_object`):

- Snowpark DataFrame / Table
- Snowpark pandas DataFrame / Series / Index
- PySpark DataFrame
- Dask DataFrame / Series / Index
- Modin DataFrame / Series
- DuckDB relation
- DB-API 2.0 cursor
- Generator functions

Where a type can't report a row count or serve a stable range (generators, some cursors), use sequential server-side loading instead of the cutoff.

### Additional Context

- Cutoff is `_MAX_UNEVALUATED_DF_ROWS = 10000` in `convert_anything_to_pandas_df`. `lazy=True` on these types currently raises `lazy-no-adapter-available`.
- Polars `LazyFrame` already has an adapter.
- Lazy dataframe spec: #15092. Implementation: #15756.
- Adjacent: #11701 (only evaluate required columns for unevaluated frames in charts).

title: `st.plotly_chart(theme=None)` still applies the active theme's font color: invisible texts on light figures in dark mode
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

With `theme=None`, the docs say Plotly's native styling is used. However, the frontend still fills
`font.color`, `font.family`, `paper_bgcolor` and `plot_bgcolor` from the active Streamlit theme,
whenever they are not explicitly set in the figure's `layout` (values from the figure's template are
ignored).

As a result, a figure that sets a white background, but leaves the font color to its template (a common
case for scientific plots meant to be exported), gets near-white texts (`#fafafa`) on that white
background in dark mode: tick labels and legend become invisible. The same figure renders fine with
`fig.show()`, and in light mode.

Related, but not the same:
- #4178
- #7955
- #6291
- #11974 (see below)

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import streamlit as st

fig = go.Figure(go.Scatter(x=[0, 1], y=[0, 1], name="data"))
# A light figure, e.g. meant to be exported: white background, font color left to the template
fig.update_layout(paper_bgcolor="white", plot_bgcolor="white", showlegend=True)

st.plotly_chart(fig, theme=None)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app above.
2. Switch Streamlit to the dark theme (⋮ menu > Settings > Dark, or set the browser / OS to
   dark mode with the default "Use system setting").
3. Reload the page (see below: the chart is not updated on a live theme switch).

### Expected Behavior

With `theme=None`, the chart renders like `fig.show()`, whatever Streamlit's light/dark theme:
dark texts on the figure's white background.

### Current Behavior

In dark mode, tick labels and legend texts are near-white (`#fafafa`) on the white background, hence
unreadable. Inspecting the layout received by Plotly (`document.querySelector('.js-plotly-plot').layout`) shows the injected values:

```json
{
  "font": {
    "color": "#fafafa",
    "family": "\"Source Sans\", sans-serif"
  },
  "paper_bgcolor": "white",
  "plot_bgcolor": "white"
}
```

Moreover, these colors are only injected at the chart's first render: they follow the theme active when
the page was loaded, not the current one (probably the same root cause as #11974, addressed by draft PR
#13854). Switching the theme without reloading leaves the chart unchanged:

| Page loaded in | Chart font color | After a live theme switch            | After a reload |
|----------------|------------------|--------------------------------------|----------------|
| light          | `#31333F`        | `#31333F` (unchanged, page is dark)  | `#fafafa`      |
| dark           | `#fafafa`        | `#fafafa` (unchanged, page is light) | `#31333F`      |

The only workaround we found is to explicitly set `font.color` (and any other of the four values above) in
every figure's layout, which is not practical for figures produced by third-party libraries. Setting
`plotly.io.templates.default` does not help: the injected layout values take precedence over the
template ones (and `import streamlit` itself sets `plotly.io.templates.default = "streamlit"`
process-wide).

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.66.1
- Plotly version: 5.24.1 (plotly.js bundled in Streamlit: 4.1.2)
- Python version: 3.13.17
- Operating System: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS
- Browser: Chromium 156


### Additional Information

Possible fixes: skip the theme color injection entirely when `theme=None`, or fall back to the figure's
template values before the active theme's ones. The colors seem to be applied in
`frontend/lib/src/components/elements/PlotlyChart/utils.ts` (as pointed out in #11031).

title: Show trends / deviations from a baseline as bars in st.dataframe cells
description: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests. - [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue. ### Summary I would like to show **trends** in `st.dataframe` as bars inside the cells. By trends I mean deviations from a reference value. The bar should start at a baseline: values below the baseline go to one side, values above it go to the other side, ideally in two colors (e.g. red / green). In most cases the baseline is 0 (for example "+12 % vs. last year"), but other baselines like a target or an average are also common. In Excel this is called "data bars". In pandas it is `Styler.bar(align=...)`. ### Why? Showing trends is a very common task in reporting tables: sales vs. last year, actual vs. plan, one item vs. the average, and so on. The user wants to see quickly in which direction a value moved and by how much. Bars that start at a baseline are the classic way to show this, but I could not find a way to do it in `st.dataframe`. `ProgressColumn` is the closest option, but it always fills the bar from `min_value`. For trend values this gives a misleading picture: ```python import pandas as pd import streamlit as st df = pd.DataFrame({ "product": ["A", "B", "C", "D"], "change_vs_lastyear": [0.12, -0.05, 0.03, -0.18], # baseline 0 "index_vs_lastyear": [112, 95, 103, 82], # baseline 100 }) st.dataframe( df, column_config={ "change_vs_lastyear": st.column_config.ProgressColumn( format="percent", min_value=-0.2, max_value=0.2, color="auto", ), "index_vs_lastyear": st.column_config.ProgressColumn( format="%d", min_value=80, max_value=120, color="auto", ), }, hide_index=True, ) ``` The screenshot shows the current `st.dataframe` output at the top. Below it is what I would expect, rendered with `st.table` + `Styler.bar(align=0)` / `Styler.bar(align=100)`. ### How? See the lower part of the screenshot above as an idea for a UI mockup. ### Additional Context - #12307: horizontal bar chart column that fills the whole cell. The examples there only show positive values starting from the left. This issue is about bars that start at a baseline (e.g. 0 or 100) and go in both directions. Both could probably be solved with the same column type. - #11014: background color of cells based on the value - #12294: positive/negative colors for `BarChartColumn` and `st.metric`

title: Console warning "Invalid color passed for textColor in theme.sidebar" whenever any custom theme option is set
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

As soon as any custom theme option is set (for example only `theme.primaryColor`), the frontend logs this warning to the browser console, once per theme evaluation:

```
Invalid color passed for textColor in theme.sidebar: ""
```

No sidebar option is configured, so the sidebar `textColor` reaches the color validator as an empty string instead of being treated as unset. Rendering is unaffected (the sidebar text gets the correct default color); it is console noise only. This looks like the same class of problem as #13831, for a field that fix did not cover.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# m.py
import streamlit as st

st.sidebar.write("side")
st.write("hi")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `streamlit run m.py --theme.primaryColor="#0D2B7A"`
2. Open the app and the browser dev tools console.
3. The warning above appears (twice on initial load in my runs).

Control: `streamlit run m.py` with no theme options logs no such warning.

### Expected Behavior

No warning when `theme.sidebar.textColor` is not set; an unset (empty) value should fall through to the default like the other sidebar colors do.

### Current Behavior

```
Invalid color passed for textColor in theme.sidebar: ""
```

Findings from narrowing it down:

| Extra options besides `theme.primaryColor` | Warning |
| --- | --- |
| none | yes |
| `theme.sidebar.primaryColor` | yes |
| `theme.textColor` | no |
| `theme.sidebar.textColor` | no |
| `theme.light.sidebar.textColor` + `theme.dark.sidebar.textColor` | no |

So the empty sidebar `textColor` seems to be inherited from the unset main `textColor` without the "unset" check that other fields get. The workarounds that silence it are not usable for apps that let users switch between light and dark at runtime: a fixed `textColor` is wrong in the other mode, and defining `[theme.light]`/`[theme.dark]` sections makes `theme.base` ignored.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Seen on 1.63.0 and 1.66.1; older versions not checked.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.66.1 (also 1.63.0)
- Python version: 3.12.12
- Operating System: macOS 15 (Darwin 24.6.0)
- Browser: Chromium (via Playwright)

### Additional Information

The message comes from the color validation helper in the frontend bundle (`utils.*.js`), which is called with `inSidebar=true` and an empty string for `textColor`.

title: Let `st.components.v2.component` serve files from a local `asset_dir` without packaging
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Custom components v2 can reference JS and CSS files by path only when the component is an installed package that declares `asset_dir` in its `pyproject.toml`. A component defined inside an app has to pass its HTML, CSS and JavaScript as inline strings. Allow `st.components.v2.component()` to take an `asset_dir` resolved relative to the calling script, so app authors can use real files without packaging. This especially helps JavaScript-only custom components, whose Python side is just the `component()` definition and whose code is written and built with JavaScript tooling.

### Why?

Inline strings work for small snippets, but they get in the way as soon as a component is built with a bundler or grows beyond one file:

- **One file only.** Inline JS can't import other files with relative paths, so there are no code-split chunks.
- **No other assets.** Fonts, images, or WASM can only be embedded as data URIs.
- **Awkward workflow.** The build output has to be read into a Python string, and editors and devtools see one long string instead of files.

The only way to use files today is to turn the component into an installed Python package. Streamlit finds a component's `asset_dir` by scanning installed distributions at startup, so a `pyproject.toml` next to the app isn't enough. For a component used in one app, that means:

- **A separate package.** It needs its own `pyproject.toml` with build-system config, a name and version, package-data rules so the JS and CSS files are included, and a `[[tool.streamlit.component.components]]` entry.
- **An install step everywhere the app runs**, for example `pip install -e ./my_component`, on every developer machine, in CI, and in every deployment. Without it, the app fails at startup.
- **Deployment workarounds.** Hosted environments install from a requirements file, so a local package needs a path dependency or publishing to a package index.

Packaging is the right model for components meant to be shared or published. For a component that belongs to one app, and especially for a JavaScript-only component with no Python code to package, it's a lot of machinery just to serve files from a folder next to the script.

### How?

Add an `asset_dir` parameter to `st.components.v2.component()`:

```python
my_component = st.components.v2.component(
    "my_component",
    js="index.js",          # relative to asset_dir
    css="styles.css",
    asset_dir="frontend",   # relative to this script
)
```

Possible rules:

- The path resolves against the file that calls `component()`, not the working directory.
- It must be an existing directory. It can't contain the calling script, so `.` and parent directories are rejected, and it can't contain `.streamlit`. This keeps app code and secrets from being served.
- If the component's package already declares an `asset_dir`, raise an error rather than guessing which to use.
- Files under the folder are watched in development, so editing them reloads the app like editing the script does.
- `asset_dir` can point straight at a bundler's output folder, such as Vite's `dist/`, so code-split chunks, fonts and images load relative to the entry file. Optionally, Streamlit could read the entry file and CSS from the bundler's manifest, so `js=` and `css=` can be left out.

### Additional Context

- The current docstring says paths and globs are "only possible for installed components".
- Related: [#15484](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15484) (AppTest discovery of installed CCv2 components).

**If you'd use this, please react with a 👍 so we can gauge interest.**

title: Community Cloud: require explicit consent before “Edit with Codespaces” commits to a repository
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Clicking “Edit with Codespaces” in Community Cloud automatically added .devcontainer/devcontainer.json to my repository’s main branch, with the commit attributed to my GitHub account. The action should preview the proposed change and require explicit consent before writing to the repository.

### Why?

I expected “Edit with Codespaces” to open a development environment. I didn’t expect it to create a commit on my default branch under my name without showing me the file or asking for confirmation.

The generated config also broke my CI since it didn't conform to my project's validation hooks.

The unexpected commit initially made me question whether someone else had accessed my account. Its attribution made it harder to identify what had actually created it.

Reviewing a repository change is useful friction. I would prefer to see the configuration the app needs and add it myself. Authorizing repository access should not replace clear consent at the point where an action modifies the repository.

### How?

Before creating a devcontainer configuration:
1. Show the exact file contents, target repository, and branch.
2. Offer a copy/download option so users can review and commit the file themselves. 
3. If automated setup is offered, require explicit confirmation and create a pull request instead of committing directly to the default branch.
4. Clearly identify Streamlit as the source of automated changes rather than attributing them solely to the user.

### Additional Context

Another user reported the same concerns about commit attribution and missing confirmation in February 2025:

https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/why-is-there-impersonation-with-added-dev-container-folder-commit/92371

The documented automatic configuration step is here:

https://docs.streamlit.io/deploy/streamlit-community-cloud/manage-your-app/edit-your-app

title: Allow setting chart selections programmatically and with a selection_default parameter
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Allow apps to set a chart's selection from Python, through session state and a `selection_default` parameter, for `st.altair_chart`, `st.vega_lite_chart`, `st.plotly_chart`, and `st.pydeck_chart`. This is the chart equivalent of what #13594 added for `st.dataframe`.

### Why?

- **Initial selections:** show a chart with a value already selected, for example the current region, or a filter restored from query parameters or a saved view.
- **Syncing views:** when a filter changes elsewhere (a widget, a dataframe selection, another chart), the chart that owns that dimension should show the same selection.
- **Undo and history:** restore a previous filter state.

Today, chart selection state is read-only, so none of this is possible. Even a selection default defined in the chart spec is ignored once `on_select="rerun"` is set (#10308).

### How?

Mirror the `st.dataframe` design from #13594:

- Accept a selection in the same schema the chart returns. For example, `st.session_state["region"] = {"selection": {"region": [{"region": "EUROPE"}]}}` for an Altair point selection, or point indices per trace for Plotly.
- Add a `selection_default` parameter for the first render.
- Validate against the chart's data and selection parameters, filtering or rejecting entries that don't apply.

Feasibility differs by chart type:

- **Plotly:** point indices per trace, plus box and lasso shapes, map well to Plotly's own selection APIs.
- **PyDeck:** object indices per layer, likely feasible.
- **Altair / Vega-Lite:** the selection Streamlit returns is simplified. A point selection carries field values, and an interval selection carries `[min, max]` per field. Vega's internal selection record needs more: which panel of the chart a selection belongs to, and the type of each field. That can be rebuilt for single-view charts with selections that declare `fields` or `encodings`. Composite charts (layer, concat, facet) and point selections without `fields`, whose values are Vega's internal row IDs, may need to stay unsupported, with a clear error.

Things to define:

- Whether a programmatic set triggers `on_select` callbacks.
- What happens when the data changes and a selected value is no longer present.
- Behavior inside forms and fragments.
- Applying the same API to `st.echarts_chart` once its selection support lands.

Clearing a selection is simpler and tracked separately in #17626.

### Additional Context

- Related: #10308, #12395 (easier cross-filtering between charts and dataframes).
- Precedent: #10128 and #13594 (setting `st.dataframe` selections programmatically).

title: Allow clearing chart selections programmatically
description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Allow apps to clear a chart's selection from Python for `st.altair_chart`, `st.vega_lite_chart`, `st.plotly_chart`, and `st.pydeck_chart`. Today, chart selection state is read-only: assigning to `st.session_state[key]` raises `StreamlitValueAssignmentNotAllowedError`, so the only way to clear a selection is to change the chart's `key`, which remounts the chart.

### Why?

Cross-filtered dashboards usually have a "Clear filters" button, or per-filter chips that remove one filter. The filter state lives in Python, but the chart that produced it keeps showing the old selection, and the selection reappears in `st.session_state[key]` on the next rerun.

The current workaround is to bump a generation counter in the chart's key:

```python
st.session_state.setdefault("gen", 0)

if st.button("Clear all"):
    st.session_state.gen += 1

event = st.altair_chart(chart, on_select="rerun", key=f"region_{st.session_state.gen}")
```

This works, but it:

- remounts the chart, which re-creates the view and costs a full re-render;
- forces apps to track per-chart key generations and to ignore stale selections from the old key; and
- is not discoverable.

`st.dataframe` already supports this since #13594: assigning `{"selection": {"rows": []}}` to its key clears the selection.

### How?

Mirror the `st.dataframe` design from #13594, limited to clearing:

- Allow assigning an empty selection to the chart's key, for example `st.session_state["region"] = {"selection": {}}`, or `None`. Non-empty values can keep raising until setting selections is supported (#17627).
- Send the clear to the frontend once, through a proto field, so the chart resets its visual selection and widget state without a remount.
- Clear the frontend's saved selection view state, so the selection does not come back after a remount or in fullscreen.

Things to define:

- Whether a programmatic clear triggers `on_select` callbacks. Widgets generally don't fire callbacks for programmatic changes.
- Behavior inside forms and fragments.
- Applying the same API to `st.echarts_chart` once its selection support lands.

### Additional Context

- Related: #12395 (easier cross-filtering between charts and dataframes), #10308 (an Altair `selection_point` default value is ignored with `on_select="rerun"`).
- Precedent: #10128 and #13594 (setting `st.dataframe` selections programmatically).

title: OmniASR: support for the Unlimited and zero-shot LLM variants
description:
### Feature request

Hi @ebezzam, thanks for adding OmniASR!

`convert_omniasr_to_hf.py` currently raises for the streaming ("Unlimited") and zero-shot LLM variants (L354–359), and frame stacking is left out because only the zero-shot variant uses it (L410).

Was this left out on purpose, for example to keep the first PR's scope down, or because the segmented generation doesn't fit Transformers' `generate` well? And is it planned?

### Motivation

As I understand the original repo, the Unlimited variants transcribe audio of any length by decoding it segment by segment, and the zero-shot variant transcribes languages it wasn't trained on from a few audio-text examples. Neither can be used from Transformers right now.

### Your contribution

If this is open, I'd be interested in contributing one of the two variants.

Separately, the integration tests only use the 300M checkpoints (`hf-audio/omniasr-llm-300m-v2` and `hf-audio/omniasr-ctc-300m-v2`), while `hf-audio` also hosts the 1B, 3B and 7B checkpoints for both. I can compare the larger ones against the original implementation and post the results here, if that's useful.

For context, I had an earlier OmniASR port for vLLM (vllm-project/vllm#36864) and wrote the multimodal requirements doc for vLLM's Transformers backend (vllm-project/vllm#65620).

title: repetition_penalty skips the first generated tokens with inputs_embeds and left padding
description:
### System Info

- `transformers` version: 5.24.0.dev0 (main at 7bf5b715a)
- Platform: Linux-6.18.44-fc-v726-x86_64-with-glibc2.39
- Python version: 3.12.3
- Huggingface_hub version: 2.4.0
- Safetensors version: 0.8.0
- Accelerate version: 1.16.0
- PyTorch version (accelerator?): 2.15.0+cu132 (NA), run on CPU
- Using distributed or parallel set-up in script?: No

### Who can help?

generate: @Cyrilvallez

### Reproduction

Generating a left-padded batch from `inputs_embeds` (no `input_ids`) with `repetition_penalty` gives different tokens for the same prompt depending on how much it is padded. Runs on CPU with a small `LlamaConfig`:

```python
import torch
from transformers import LlamaConfig, LlamaForCausalLM

torch.manual_seed(14)
config = LlamaConfig(
    vocab_size=64, hidden_size=32, intermediate_size=64, num_hidden_layers=2,
    num_attention_heads=4, num_key_value_heads=2, pad_token_id=0, bos_token_id=None, eos_token_id=None,
)
model = LlamaForCausalLM(config).eval()
embed = model.get_input_embeddings()
kwargs = dict(max_new_tokens=8, do_sample=False, repetition_penalty=2.0)

# Same prompt, alone and left-padded in a batch
alone = torch.tensor([[5, 6]])
batch = torch.tensor([[0, 0, 0, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9, 10, 11]])

out_alone = model.generate(inputs_embeds=embed(alone), attention_mask=torch.ones_like(alone), **kwargs)
out_batch = model.generate(inputs_embeds=embed(batch), attention_mask=(batch != 0).long(), **kwargs)
print("alone:   ", out_alone[0].tolist())
print("batched: ", out_batch[0].tolist())
```

Output on main (7bf5b715a). The padded row repeats token 34 four times despite `repetition_penalty=2.0`:

```
alone:    [34, 14, 21, 48, 13, 8, 39, 45]
batched:  [34, 34, 34, 34, 16, 19, 20, 31]
```

Cause: since #50149 (first bad commit 0f5a2a5bc, outputs match on its parent), `_get_logits_processor` in `generation/utils.py` passes each row's left-padding length from the attention mask to `RepetitionPenaltyLogitsProcessor` as `prompt_ignore_length`. With only `inputs_embeds`, `input_ids` holds just the generated tokens, so the first N generated tokens of a row with N pad tokens are never penalized.

I have a one-line fix with a regression test ready (only compute the padding lengths when the prompt is in `input_ids`) and can open a PR once this is triaged.

### Expected behavior

The padded prompt should generate the same tokens as the unpadded one, as it did before #50149:

```
alone:    [34, 14, 21, 48, 13, 8, 39, 45]
batched:  [34, 14, 21, 48, 13, 8, 39, 45]
```

The warning `generate` already emits for this case also says the penalty applies "only to newly generated tokens, not to the prompt", so all generated tokens should be penalized.

title: `GenerationMixin.generate()` mutates caller-provided `encoder_outputs` during beam search and multi-return sampling
description:
### System Info
Transformers: `5.24.0.dev0` | PyTorch: `2.11.0+cu130` | Linux | CPU and NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU  
Upstream commit: `2f1bc5e321b9a736200a590d6e7743ccdeb60772`

### Who can help?
@Cyrilvallez

### Reproduction
`generate()` modifies caller-provided `encoder_outputs` in place during beam search or multi-return sampling. The first call works, but reusing the same outputs can silently return the wrong number of sequences or raise an indexing error.

This reproducer uses a randomly initialized T5 model on CPU, without downloading checkpoints.

```python
import torch
from transformers import T5Config, T5ForConditionalGeneration

torch.manual_seed(42)
config = T5Config(
    vocab_size=64, d_model=32, d_kv=8, d_ff=64,
    num_layers=1, num_decoder_layers=1, num_heads=4,
    dropout_rate=0.0, pad_token_id=0, eos_token_id=1,
    decoder_start_token_id=0,
)
model = T5ForConditionalGeneration(config).eval()
ids = torch.randint(3, 60, (2, 8))
mask = torch.ones_like(ids)

with torch.no_grad():
    enc = model.get_encoder()(input_ids=ids, attention_mask=mask, return_dict=True)
    print("Before:", tuple(enc.last_hidden_state.shape))
    first = model.generate(
        encoder_outputs=enc, attention_mask=mask,
        num_beams=3, num_return_sequences=2,
        max_new_tokens=4, use_cache=False,
    )
    print("After:", tuple(enc.last_hidden_state.shape))
    print("First output batch:", first.shape[0])
    reused = model.generate(
        encoder_outputs=enc, attention_mask=mask,
        num_beams=1, max_new_tokens=4, use_cache=False,
    )
    print("Reused batch:", reused.shape[0])
    print("Expected batch:", ids.shape[0])
```

**Output:**
```text
Before: (2, 8, 32)
After: (6, 8, 32)
First output batch: 4
Reused batch: 6
Expected batch: 2
```

The original encoder batch is expanded from 2 to 6, so the next generation incorrectly returns six sequences instead of two.

### Some Confirmations
I confirmed the same behavior using the pretrained `google/flan-t5-small` checkpoint with two English-to-German translation prompts. After generating with three beams, the original encoder shape changed from `(2, 13, 512)` to `(6, 13, 512)`. Reusing it produced six translations instead of two, with outputs that differed from the reference. With the fix, the shape remained `(2, 13, 512)`, and both returned translations matched the reference.

I also searched public GitHub code. Examples include [Exemplary Empathy](https://github.com/declare-lab/exemplary-empathy/blob/887f0c2d4023824674aaeaa6a059b293f9ee35d2/models.py#L219-L240) (T5 with eight beams), [NMRTrans](https://github.com/little1d/NMRTrans/blob/9a72756532e60d540f05eafa93d31aecd1cb4362/src/model.py#L1219-L1255) (T5 with a fallback that can retry using the same encoder outputs), [Musyn](https://github.com/trekar99/musyn/blob/7cecb7e8820205b63fcfa7eead855f2cc6fa35f0/model/bart.py#L120-L150) (audio-conditioned BART with beam search), and [Chatbot API](https://github.com/Trungpham2k4/chatbot-api/blob/df8cf402b39bb67990ba23833aaa50bf7482b37c/app.py#L89) (projected encoder features with three beams).

These examples show real usage across dialogue, translation, and multimodal applications. They are not all confirmed failures, and the GitHub search is not a statistical measure of production prevalence. The main risk occurs when applications reuse or inspect encoder outputs after expansion, particularly in retry or multi-decoding workflows.

### Additional testing
I tested six encoder-decoder architectures: **T5, BART, mBART, Pegasus, Marian, and Blenderbot**, covering 120 configurations with greedy decoding, beam search, multi-return sampling, caching on/off, and padded/unpadded inputs.

| Result | Unpatched | Patched |
|---|---:|---:|
| Configurations | 120 | 120 |
| Encoder-output mutations | 96 | 0 |
| Wrong reused batch sizes | 48 | 0 |
| Errors | 48 | 0 |
| Fully correct cases | 24 | 120 |

The 96 mutations include cases that subsequently failed during reuse. The patch passed **120/120 CPU and 120/120 GPU configurations**. Three additional regression cases also passed locally: two tiny-T5 decoding cases and one pretrained FLAN-T5 test.


In `src/transformers/generation/utils.py`, `_expand_inputs_for_generation()` passes the original `encoder_outputs` to `_expand_dict_for_generation()`, which replaces its tensor entries in place. This unintentionally modifies the caller-owned `ModelOutput`.

### Suggested fix
Shallow-copy `encoder_outputs` before expanding its tensors. This preserves the original container without deep-copying the encoder activations. 

### Expected behavior
`generate()` should expand encoder outputs internally without modifying the caller's object. An original batch of 2 should remain 2 after generation, and reusing those encoder outputs should produce the same deterministic results as freshly computed equivalents. This should hold across supported encoder-decoder architectures, decoding modes, cache settings, and padded inputs.

title: Prompt lookup decoding crashes with static cache near max_length
description:
### System Info

- transformers 5.24.0.dev0 (main, installed from git today)
- torch 2.14.1+cpu
- Python 3.13, Google Colab, CPU

### Who can help?

@Cyrilvallez

### Reproduction

Since #49415 landed, `prompt_lookup_num_tokens` + `cache_implementation="static"` crashes when the lookup finds a match in the last few steps of generation.

Repro on `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` (transformers 5.24.0.dev0 from main, torch 2.14.1, CPU, Colab):

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

name = "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct"
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(name, dtype=torch.float32).eval()
msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": "Repeat this sentence exactly, word for word: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog while the farmer watches from the old red barn near the river."}]
ids = tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, add_generation_prompt=True, return_tensors="pt", return_dict=True)["input_ids"]

for n in (10, 15, 20, 25, 30):
    kw = dict(max_new_tokens=n, do_sample=False)
    greedy = model.generate(ids, cache_implementation="static", **kw)
    try:
        out = model.generate(ids, prompt_lookup_num_tokens=10, cache_implementation="static", **kw)
        print(n, "ok, matches greedy:", torch.equal(greedy, out))
    except Exception as e:
        print(n, "CRASH:", type(e).__name__, e)
```

```
10 CRASH: IndexError index_copy_(): index 69 is out of bounds for dimension 2 with size 69
15 CRASH: IndexError index_copy_(): index 74 is out of bounds for dimension 2 with size 74
20 CRASH: IndexError index_copy_(): index 79 is out of bounds for dimension 2 with size 79
25 ok, matches greedy: True
30 ok, matches greedy: True
```

### Expected behavior

Prompt lookup + static cache should give the same output as plain greedy (it does at 25 and 30 above), not crash.

I think the cause is in `PromptLookupCandidateGenerator.get_candidates`: `end_idx = min(end_idx, input_length, self.max_length)` is supposed to stop drafts at `max_length - 1`, but `end_idx` indexes into the prompt, so comparing it with `max_length` never does anything. Near the end it drafts up to N tokens past the end, and the static cache only has `max_length - 1` slots. With a dynamic cache those tokens just get trimmed, which is probably why nobody noticed. `AssistedCandidateGenerator` already caps this correctly (`max_length - cur_len - 1`).

I know #46993/#47195 tried the same cap before. Back then it only caused extra tokens, but now it's a hard crash with static cache. Happy to open a PR with the 2-line fix and a regression test (tiny config, fails on main, passes with the fix) if that works for you.
